title: Hover, active, focus and disabled
summary: One button styled through its states with :hover, :active, :focus-visible and an aria-disabled selector.
explanation: Each state is a pseudo-class on the same selector: :hover while the pointer is over it, :active while it is pressed, :focus-visible when it has keyboard focus. Order matters when two apply at once: :active comes after :hover so a pressed button shows its pressed look.
The disabled look uses an attribute selector, [aria-disabled="true"]. It has the same specificity as a pseudo-class, and it is listed last, so its grey wins over the hover colour.
Hover, press and Tab through the buttons in the preview to see each state.
tryThis: Hover and press the first button; press Tab to see the focus ring.
Move the :hover rule below :active: pressing no longer looks different while hovering.
Remove the cursor: not-allowed line, then hover the disabled button.
